text.p: France coach Aime Jacquet included six players of French league leaders Monaco in a squad of 37 on Tuesday to gather on Saturday for training and a series of tests and medical check-ups.

It is from this list that Jacquet will pick a reduced squad of 18 on Monday for the friendly international against Sweden at Parc des Princes on April 2 and, nearer the date, his squad for the World Cup warm-up Tournament of France in June.
Jacquet has taken advantage of the fact that there is no league football in Europe's major leagues this weekend to gather all his potential World Cup players for a spell together.
UEFA Cup semifinalists Monaco's fine form was rewarded with first ever call-ups for teenage striker Thierry Henry and midfielders Sylvain Legwinski and Emmanuel Petit.
Monaco defenders Patrick Blondeau and Martin Djetou and goalkeeper Fabien Barthez were also included.
Goalkeepers - Fabien Barthez (Monaco), Lionel Charbonnier (Auxerre), Bernard Lama (Paris St Germain), Lionel Letizi (Metz), Christophe Revault (Le Havre)

Defenders - Laurent Blanc (Barcelona), Patrick Blondeau (Monaco), Vincent Candela (AS Roma), Marcel Desailly (AC Milan), Alain Goma (Auxerre), Pierre Laigle (Sampdoria), Franck Lebouef (Chelsea), Bixente Lizarazu (Athletic Bilbao), Bruno N'Gotty (PSG), Lilian Thuram (Parma)

Midfielders - Didier Deschamps (Juventus), Martin Djetou (Monaco), Franck Gava (Lyon), Christian Karembeu (Sampdoria), Sabri Lamouchi (Auxerre), Sylvain Legwinski (Monaco), Claude Makelele (Nantes), Emmanuel Petit (Monaco), Patrick Vieira (Arsenal), Zinedine Zidane (Juventus)

Forwards - Ibrahim Ba (Bordeaux), Youri Djorkaeff (Inter Milan), Bernard Diomede (Auxerre), Christophe Dugarry (AC Milan), Thierry Henry (Monaco), Marc Keller (Karlsruhe), Lilian Laslandes (Auxerre), Patrice Loko (PSG), Florian Maurice (Lyon), Nicolas Ouedec (Espanyol), Reynald Pedros (Parma), Robert Pires (Metz).
